newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 3.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in South Korea's leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- After questioning Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo, prosecutors are set to summon bankers this week over a loan scandal involving the conglomerate's steelmaking flagship.
- Some Hanbo Steel executives said the actual amount of investment in the company's new mill in Tangjin is less than figures earlier released by the company.
- President Kim Young-sam called the Hanbo loan scandal as a typical example of corruption, and said the country's future would be dismal unless corruption was eradicated.
- Foreign diplomatic missions in South Korea have asked the Seoul government to guarantee that the Hanbo Group's construction projects overseas will be carried out without setbacks.
- Despite this week's Lunar New Year, sales have fallen to lows, due to a combination of cold weather, recent industrial strife, and the Hanbo Group's financial failure.
